statements.statement: Both papers B and C emphasize the use of mid-level representations and simulation environments to facilitate autonomous driving research.
Paper B highlights that mid-level representations enable training on real or simulated data and facilitate closed-loop simulation testing before real deployment.
Paper C describes CARLA as an open-source simulator supporting development, training, and validation of autonomous urban driving systems.
Paper C supports flexible specification of sensor suites and environmental conditions.
This theme shows a shared focus on leveraging simulation and mid-level abstractions to improve autonomous driving model training and evaluation.

parsed.type_evidence: Claims 1 and 2 both discuss simulation environments for training and validation, but only claim 1 discusses mid-level representations. There is no claim from Paper C about mid-level representations.
